review.tagline: Terminal coding agent with LSP, debugger, subagents and in-process tools
review.summary: oh-my-pi (omp) is a terminal coding agent forked from Pi, written in TypeScript with a Rust core and run on Bun. It ships 31 built-in tools, including hashline content-hash edits, LSP and DAP debugger access, persistent Python/JS eval cells, parallel subagents in isolated worktrees, and in-process ripgrep and coreutils. It supports 60+ model providers and can run inside Zed over ACP.
review.audience: Developers wanting a terminal coding agent with IDE-level tooling
strengths: LSP and DAP integration: renames go through the language server, debuggers can be stepped
Subagents run in isolated worktrees and return schema-validated results
In-process grep, glob and 58 coreutils; same binary on macOS, Linux and Windows
Reads existing Cursor, Cline, Codex and Copilot rule files without conversion
weaknesses: Benchmark gains cited come from the author's own blog post, not independent tests
Large tool surface (31 tools, 16 URL schemes) takes time to learn
Fork of Pi, so upstream changes are tracked separately
PR policy is a temporary trial and may return to vouch-only
needs: Needs Bun >= 1.3.14 (or prebuilt binary), LLM provider API access
Models: 60+ providers, Grok, Gemini, MiniMax, OpenAI Codex
